Triangulated surfaces in three dimensions

Source: R/layers-surface.R
geom_surface_3d.Rd

Grid surfaces estimate vertex normals from height differences along each axis. With shading = "flat" lighting uses the normalised mean of each face's vertex normals and a numeric fill is averaged over each face. With shading = "smooth" the vertex normals are interpolated across each face (Phong 1975) and a fill that varies between vertices is interpolated in linear light (Gouraud 1971), as MATLAB's lighting gouraud with FaceColor = "interp" and rgl's smooth material.

Usage

geom_surface_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "grid",
  max_edge = Inf,
  shade = TRUE,
  wireframe = FALSE,
  hidden = "hide",
  outline = NULL,
  alpha_mode = "face",
  shading = "flat",
  material = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_surface_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "grid",
  max_edge = Inf,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments.

method

Grid connectivity or Delaunay triangulation.

max_edge

Maximum triangle edge length in transformed x/y units.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

wireframe

Whether to draw triangle edges.

hidden

Hidden stroke policy.

outline

Feature lines from outline_3d(), or NULL for none.

alpha_mode

How a translucent surface composites. "face" blends every face over what lies behind it, so a surface seen through itself darkens where it folds over. "surface" paints each sheet (a connected set of faces sharing vertices, such as one isosurface level) as one translucent film: other sheets show through it, its own pieces behind its nearer pieces do not. A sheet of several fill colours needs a device with Porter-Duff groups and alpha masks (ragg, cairo_pdf, svg); other devices, pdf() among them, paint it as "face". The raster and hybrid backends keep, per sample, the nearest piece of each sheet and composite the sheets in depth order, with any fill colours; so does the view_3d() viewer. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), stat_parametric_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

shading

"flat" lights and fills each face uniformly; "smooth" interpolates vertex normals and vertex fills across faces. The raster backend and the view_3d() viewer interpolate per sample, perspective correctly. The vector backend draws a face whose colour varies as one linear gradient when its colour varies along one direction and the device supports gradients, and otherwise as flat sub-triangles whose colours differ from the interpolated colour by at most the option ggplot3d.shading_tolerance (default 2 / 255 in encoded sRGB), splitting each triangle at most eight times (256 pieces along an edge), which can leave larger steps where a channel approaches black and the sRGB curve is steepest. Gradients follow the sRGB curve through their stops within the same tolerance. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

material

Surface material from material_3d(): ambient, diffuse and specular strengths, shininess and an optional back-side colour. NULL reflects ambient and diffuse light fully, with no highlight.

geom

Geom prototype used to draw the computed triangles.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6))
d$z <- with(d, x^2 + y^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z))
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "steelblue") + coord_3d()
p + stat_surface_3d() + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = z), shading = "smooth") + coord_3d()
